merge.title: Merge into a variable font
merge.intro: Several weights of the same font are in the list: you can combine them into a single variable file.
merge.how1: A variable font holds every weight in a single file. Fontshift builds it from your files: each one serves as a reference point (for example Light and Bold), and the weights in between are calculated from them.
merge.how2: This only works if every character is drawn the same way in all the files: same points, in the same order. Fontshift checks this before merging. If it isn’t the case, it refuses rather than create a faulty font, and converts the files separately.
merge.limit1: The font only spans the weights you provide: with Light and Bold, there is no Thin or Black.
merge.limit2: The weights in between are calculated: they may differ slightly from the official files. Add every weight you have for a closer result.
merge.limit3: Upright and italic styles give two separate variable fonts.
merge.limit4: Many commercial fonts are refused: their files are often adjusted one by one when exported.
merge.limit5: Make sure the font’s license allows it to be modified.
merge.ok: Compatible: can become a single variable file ({range}).
merge.okOn: These {count} files will become a single variable file ({range}).
merge.errIncompatible: Can’t merge: {count, plural, one {# character is not drawn} other {# characters are not drawn}} the same way from one file to the next{chars}.
merge.errGlyphSet: Can’t merge: the files don’t contain the same characters ({count, plural, one {# difference} other {# differences}}).
merge.errSameStyle: Can’t merge: {files} have the same weight ({weight}). Remove one of them.
merge.errMixed: Can’t merge: the list mixes TTF and OTF files of this font. Keep a single type.
merge.errOther: Can’t merge: these files are not compatible.
